content:
Apple's first foldable iPhone is expected to launch in about two weeks. Despite potentially being named the "iPhone Ultra" and carrying a price tag of over $2,000, it will come with several major compromises.

#1: Telephoto Lens

According to reports, the iPhone Ultra will feature two cameras, including a main lens and an ultra-wide lens, but is not expected to include a telephoto lens. For many people, this may be the device's biggest design compromise.

The iPhone Ultra's main and ultra-wide cameras are both expected to be 48-megapixel, similar to the current base model iPhone 17.

#2: Action Button

According to multiple leaked iPhone Ultra dummy units, the device will not feature an Action Button. In fact, this will be the first iPhone from Apple to completely lack any mute switch.

The dummy units show that the left edge of the device is completely blank. Reportedly, the side button and camera control button will be located on the right edge of the iPhone Ultra. The volume buttons will be placed on the top edge of the device, similar to the iPad mini.

#3: Face ID

The iPhone Ultra is not expected to feature Face ID, instead incorporating Touch ID into the side button. This will be the first iPhone without Face ID since Apple first introduced it with the iPhone X in 2017.

Apple's choice of Touch ID over Face ID on the iPhone Ultra is likely due to the device's ultra-thin design. Additionally, Apple would need to include two sets of Face ID components, one for the outer display and one for the inner display.

Apple still uses Touch ID built into the power button on most of its iPads, including the basic iPad, iPad mini, and iPad Air.

#4: MagSafe

Although Apple could surprise us at any time, the iPhone Ultra does not appear to support MagSafe wireless charging. The back of the leaked iPhone Ultra dummy units does not show the MagSafe magnetic ring.

The iPhone Ultra may offer standard wireless charging similar to the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 foldable phone. However, based on current rumours, the likelihood of MagSafe support seems slim.

#5: Physical SIM Card

According to sources including Tianfeng Securities analyst Ming-Chi Kuo and Bloomberg, the iPhone Ultra will support eSIM only globally.

This is likely due to the ultra-thin design of the foldable iPhone. The iPhone Air also features an extremely slim body and supports eSIM only globally. As for the iPhone 17 and iPhone 17 Pro, they support eSIM only in the US and some other countries, but retain a physical SIM card slot in markets such as China.

Summary

It's clear that Apple's foldable iPhone Ultra will come with several significant trade-offs. The question is whether the practicality of this innovative foldable design is enough to compensate for the other limitations.

Personally, I'm very much looking forward to trying out the iPhone Ultra hands-on. The trade-off that concerns me most is the lack of MagSafe. I'm currently using the iPhone Air, so I've already gotten used to life without a telephoto lens. I'm also confident I can quickly adapt to Touch ID. However, I've placed MagSafe chargers all over my home, so switching back to standard wireless charging or long-term wired charging will be a major adjustment.

What do you think? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
